romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel was rejected due to not feeling a need for salvation, making their own traditions, pride, and misunderstanding of the law.
key_points: Did not feel need for salvation.
Made own traditions and worshipped them.
Proud and self righteous.
Misunderstood their own law.
sections: Israel rejections — Reasons for their rejection 1-13

related.title: Law S True Function
related.why: This note explains that the law's true purpose is to point to the savior, contrasting the rejection reason of misunderstanding the law with its actual function.

related.title: Remedy for Rejection
related.why: This note provides the practical solution to the rejection issue by detailing the missionary program and the necessary relationship between believing and obeying.

related.title: Consequences of Rejection
related.why: This note addresses the consequence of rejection by explaining Israel's guilt and the sharing of the message with Gentiles, which relates to the broader context of rejection.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: The law is a signpost leading to the savior, requiring obedience in the heart rather than just outward action.
key_points: Law is a signpost.
Law leads the sinner to the savior.
Must be obeyed in the heart.
Difference between obeying Lord and calling on Lord.
sections: Israel rejections — Reasons for their rejection 1-13

related.title: Israel S Rejection Reasons
related.why: This note explains why Israel failed to fulfill the law, contrasting the outward action with the necessary internal obedience.

related.title: Remedy for Rejection
related.why: This note details the necessary steps (hearing the message) required to overcome the rejection of the law.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: The remedy involves a missionary program and clarifies the relationship between believing and obeying, emphasizing that one must first hear.
key_points: Used for missionary program.
Believing and obeying are interchangeable.
To believe one must first hear.
sections: Remedy for Rejection 14-17

related.title: Israel S Rejection Reasons
related.why: This note explains the root causes of rejection, which informs the need for the remedy.

related.title: Law S True Function
related.why: Understanding the true function of the law is necessary to grasp the required obedience mentioned in the remedy.

related.title: Consequences of Rejection
related.why: This note details the outcome of rejection, providing context for why the missionary program is the remedy.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel is guilty because they did hear, and the message is shared with Gentiles, though God still yearns for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty because they DID hear.
Message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel rejection.
God still yearns for His people.
sections: Results of their rejection 18-21

related.title: Israel S Rejection Reasons
related.why: This note explains the specific reasons why Israel faced rejection, which directly informs the broader concept of the consequences of rejection.

related.title: Remedy for Rejection
related.why: This note outlines the practical steps and theological framework for addressing the consequences of rejection, such as the missionary program and clarifying the relationship between believing and obeying.

related.title: Law S True Function
related.why: Understanding the true function of the law helps contextualize why Israel's adherence to it was insufficient for salvation, linking back to the reasons for their rejection.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Romans 12:1 is the basis for other relationships discussed in this section, stemming from the preceding theological points about condemnation, justification, and assurance.
key_points: Romans 3:20 is the 'therefore' of condemnation.
Romans 5:1 is the 'therefore' of justification.
Romans 8:1 is the 'therefore' of assurance.
Romans 12:1 is the 'therefore' of dedication.
sections: Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides the practical application of dedicating the body as a living sacrifice, which is the core concept of Romans 12:1.

related.title: Mind As Sacrifice
related.why: Understanding the mind as a sacrifice explains how the internal transformation mentioned in Romans 12:1 is achieved through the Holy Spirit.

related.title: Will As Sacrifice
related.why: This note details how surrendering the will is a necessary component of the dedication process outlined in Romans 12:1.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The body is a living sacrifice to give to God, exemplified by Isaac's obedience and Jesus Christ's sacrifice.
key_points: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God.
Isaac died in obedience to God, yielding to God’s will.
Jesus Christ actually died in sacrifice.
sections: Dedication - 3 steps > Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God

related.title: Basis for Dedication
related.why: This note explains the theological foundation that connects the concept of the body as a living sacrifice to other aspects of Christian dedication.

related.title: Mind As Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides a specific example of how the concept of a 'living sacrifice' applies to the internal state of the mind.

related.title: Will As Sacrifice
related.why: This note details how surrendering the will functions as a practical application of offering one's will as a living sacrifice to God.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The mind is a sacrifice to God, and the Holy Spirit changes the mind by releasing inner power, leading to spiritual transformation.
key_points: The world wants to change your mind with external pressure.
If God controls your thinking, you are a transformer.
Meditating on God’s Word makes you more spiritual.
sections: Dedication - 3 steps > Your mind is a sacrifice to God

related.title: Will As Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains how surrendering the will to God is a sacrifice that grants willpower, which is directly related to the mind being changed by the Holy Spirit.

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides a concrete example of a living sacrifice (the body) to God, which complements the idea of the mind being a sacrifice to God.

related.title: God S Perfect Plan
related.why: Understanding God's perfect plan provides the context for why the mind is a sacrifice and how the Holy Spirit's work leads to spiritual transformation.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: The will is a sacrifice to God, and surrendering it to God allows His power to take over, which provides willpower.
key_points: Your mind controls your body, your will controls your mind.
Yielding our will to God gives us willpower.
Surrender happens through disciplined prayer.
Pray about everything and yield plans to Him.

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: This note provides a concrete example of how the concept of sacrifice is applied to the physical body.

related.title: Mind As Sacrifice
related.why: This note explains the mechanism by which surrendering the will leads to the acquisition of spiritual power.

related.title: God S Perfect Plan
related.why: Understanding God's perfect plan provides the ultimate context for why surrendering the will is the correct response.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Each Christian must honestly evaluate their spiritual gifts and ministry, avoiding both under and over-evaluation as examples of pride.
key_points: Each Christian must identify spiritual gifts and ministry.
Be honest about self-evaluation.
Both under and over-evaluation are examples of pride.
sections: Relationship (to other believers) > Honest evaluation

related.title: Faith Hope Love
related.why: This note provides the ultimate framework for evaluating spiritual gifts and ministry by emphasizing love as the greatest element.

related.title: Loving Participation
related.why: This note directly relates to the honest evaluation of ministry by stressing the importance of having an honest, humble love when engaging with others.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Work with others even if you don't like them, recognizing that no gift is superior, and gifts are tools to build with.
key_points: Work with others even if you don’t like them.
No one gift is better or greater than others.
Gifts are tools to build with, not toys or weapons.
sections: Relationship (to other believers) > Faithful cooperation

related.title: Loving Participation
related.why: This note directly relates to the idea of working with others by emphasizing the necessary attitude of having an honest, humble love and sharing burdens.

related.title: Relationship to Enemies
related.why: This note provides a practical framework for cooperating with those who are difficult by showing how returning good in exchange for evil requires love.

related.title: Honest Evaluation
related.why: This note supports the 'no gift is superior' aspect of faithful cooperation by advising Christians to honestly evaluate their gifts to avoid pride.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Attitude matters in loving participation, which involves having an honest, humble love and sharing the burdens of others.
key_points: Attitude matters.
Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body.
Have an honest, humble love, not hypocritical love.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer.
Share the burdens of others.
sections: Relationship (to other believers) > Loving participation

related.title: Faith Hope Love
related.why: This note emphasizes love as the greatest element, which is central to the attitude required for loving participation.

related.title: Living Sacrifice
related.why: Understanding the body as a living sacrifice connects to the active, humble, and self-giving nature of loving participation.

related.title: Honest Evaluation
related.why: Honest evaluation of spiritual gifts prevents pride, which is a key attitude that must be present in loving participation.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Returning good in exchange for evil requires love, and viewing justice as love is the way to approach enemies.
key_points: Returning good in exchange for evil requires love.
Having enemies because of impatience and lack of love is different from following Christ.
View justice as love rather than positioning yourself as better or less deserving of justice.

related.title: Faith Hope Love
related.why: This note emphasizes love as the greatest element, which is central to the concept of approaching enemies with love.

related.title: Loving Participation
related.why: This note discusses the attitude required in loving participation, which involves having an honest, humble love necessary for dealing with difficult relationships.

related.title: God S Perfect Plan
related.why: Understanding God's perfect plan provides the ultimate framework for how to view and approach enemies through the lens of divine purpose.

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms: freedom from judgment, freedom from defeat, freedom from discouragement, and freedom from separation.
key_points: Freedom from judgment (No condemnation).
Freedom from defeat (No obligation; submit to God).
Freedom from discouragement (No frustration).
Freedom from separation.
sections: Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary — Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin, but it is not useless, and believers experience groans from creation, believers, and the Holy Spirit.
key_points: Creation groans (18-22): Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin but is not useless; pain leads to something beautiful and ends.
Believers groan (23-25): Believers have a taste of glory but are anxious to get there.
Holy Spirit groans (23-30): The Spirit groans but also prays on our behalf.
sections: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Believers groan (23-25)

romans-08-study-notes.summary: God is always at work and has a perfect plan for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
key_points: God is always at work (verse 28).
God has a perfect plan (verse 29) for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.
Predestination applies only to saved people (Point to be discussed).

key_points: Faith, hope, and love remain (1 Corinthians 13:13).
Love is the greatest of these three.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1).
